messages.text: Can we make the pinecone house at recess tomorrow? I found a flat rock for the door.
Yes and we can let Ava put the leaf roof on if she wants. She looked sad by the swings.
Okay. You bring the tiny sticks and I will draw the map after math.
Deal. We can make room for Tyler's car road when I show him after dinner.
My mom said we can bring the magic forest pictures tomorrow.
Good. I am going to draw mine after I try my two lines again.
I can stand by you before Mrs. Bell calls our table.
Ok. If my voice gets tiny I will look at the trees on my paper.
I put your water bottle by the back door. We can just watch the first few minutes if you want.
Can I stand by Emma first? My socks feel bunchy with the hard pads.
Yep. Coach said nobody has to jump in right away. We'll fix the pads when we park.
I put two sparkly stars on my bottle so I can find it.
I saw your face when the bus doors opened. I will be by the car with your blue folder.
Can I sit by you before Tyler shows me his dinosaur noise?
Yes. He can tell Dad first. Your sticker page is zipped in my purse until you ask for it.
Also my bridge middle keeps falling. Can Dad see it after supper?
I put the red berries on the counter to thaw a little. Please leave the big pitcher where it is until I come in.
Rain is getting heavier, so stay inside after homework. Bring me your reading folder first.
Can I peel the banana now?
Can I do the book with the map pages and the castle after my spelling words?
Yes, peel it and put it by your pink cup. I will do the noisy button after I wash my hands.
Yes, two chapters. Then I will check if there is time for the snowman movie before dinner.
I will put my bookmark by the part with the tower.
I put the blue notebook back in your folder. The moon helmet page and the puppy checkup page are both tucked inside.
Can I add the little people talking before dinner? The blank spot looks too quiet.
Yes, after spelling practice. Keep the markers at the kitchen table so Tyler does not grab them.
Ok. I want the room on the page to look like the one I was thinking of.
Can I do the rocket numbers on the family tablet after spelling?
Yes, after spelling words are checked. Set the kitchen timer for 20 minutes, please.
Can I show Emma my score?
Take a picture and I can send it to her mom later.
Tyler wants you to know he saved you the blue car. He also says the TV had a big street crowd again.
Were they the people with signs? I only know the words because Mrs. Bell said sometimes signs mean someone wants people to listen.
Yes, signs like that. We can talk after dinner, and you can tell Tyler the blue car still has to take turns.
Tyler says his red car needs the long gray road again.
Okay. If somebody says something is hurting them, the other people should stop and listen.
Only if he does not drive through the blue pieces. That is where the hidden path starts.
He is nodding. He wants the little people to go past the tall towers first.
They have to cross the water bridge before the sister with the crown can find the path.
Are you bringing the blue bag today? I can stand by you near the fence.
Maybe. I get quiet when there are kids I do not know.
We can just pass back and forth. Coach said nobody has to get it right.
Okay. If you wave first I will come over.
My mom found the video with the giant lit-up castle and music again.
Can we draw that one tomorrow and the one from my book with the tall white towers?
Yes. Bring pink crayons. I will make the road go all the way across the paper.
I will make our car tiny so it looks like we are really going there.
I'm at Hy-Vee. For Friday pizza, do you want the red peppers, yellow corn, spinach, and black olives again?
Yes please, and can the pieces go in stripes?
Stripes are fine. I already have the little pepperoni slices at home.
Can we put some sweet yellow chunks on my side too?
Mom typed this. Can me and Melissa look for red birds after snack?
Yes but I want to bring the blue cup for the worm if he is on the sidewalk again.
Mom says only by the porch steps and not past the little tree.
Ok I will wave from there before we go to the grass.
Tyler wants to know if the cake can have eight candles and sprinkles this time.
Yes and purple frosting. He can help put cars on the table but not touch my stickers.
Deal. We will talk about it after we get back from the Council Bluffs errand.
Tyler wants to know if the shiny quarters on your desk are for the pink thing with the slot.
Yes but he cannot shake it. I need those for later.
I moved them up high. The glitter marker set can stay on your birthday paper for now.
Okay. I drew the markers with stars so I remember.
You left the truck even after you watched from the door for a bit. That was enough for today.
I almost stayed there. Then Emma waved and I kicked one ball.
One kick counts. We can wash the grass off your shoes after supper.
I put the signed soccer paper in your red folder. The clinic page was easy this year.
Did you check the box that says I don't take anything every morning?
Yes. I also wrote that stage-light nerves got better with breathing and Mrs. Bell's practice.
Good because I want to play at recess and not talk about the assembly all morning.
Melissa kept her place on the card today and tried the last sentence with the group.
I made the castle part on my paper too.
I noticed. Tomorrow we will stand by the blue tape again, and you can use the same slow start.
Melissa kept her finger under each line today and finished the last page before packing up.
I read the fox part but I almost skipped a word.
You caught it and fixed it. Please bring the blue folder back Monday so we can use the same partner chart.
Okay. Emma and I know where our names go.
Put the blue folder in your backpack. Mrs. Bell said the nurse note needs to go home and then to Dr. Jensen.
Can I ask you first if the arm thing is today
Yes, ask me at breakfast, and we will ask Dr. Jensen too. Dad packed your purple bandage in the side pocket.
I want the smoothie after if I do the brave squeeze
We saw the Bell girls at the grocery checkout. Mrs. Bell said your reading paper is tucked in the blue folder.
Did Emma see the sprinkle cookies?
She did, and her mom asked if you still know the clap-clap song from Sunday morning.
I know it. Can we play the clean dance videos after supper too?
Tyler wanted to send you a car picture before we go to church supper. Your blue folder made it home.
Tell him I saw it. I have to read the fox page before we leave.
He says vroom. Shoes by the bench at 5:10, and bring the paper with your lines.
Okay. Can I show him one soccer kick outside if it is still warm?
My mom said I can be on the same line as you again if Coach lets us.
Good because last time I almost stayed in the car but then you waved.
Bring the shiny sticker sheet. We can put dots by our names after snack.
Okay and I know which way the shin guards go now.
Parade parking is by the church lot. If we get split up, go to the library steps like we practiced.
I mowed around the far maple, so stay off the loose sticks by the trunk.
Can I ask the man by the shiny car too if I can't see you?
Can I still go behind it where the tall grass makes the tiny path?
Yep, the one helping with the cones. But first stay with Mom and hold Tyler's mitten.
Behind it is fine. Keep your shoes on and come back when Mom calls lunch.
Tyler says the car lights are for the candy line.
Tyler wants to chase me first, then I am going to the path.
The big envelope on the kitchen counter is mine and Dad's, so please leave it there after you get your crayons.
Is it like the cup at school where we put papers in?
A little, but this one is a grown-up chore. Your class cup is for school choices, and Mrs. Bell helps everyone be fair.
Dad said the TV people were being loud so I went back to my castle drawing.
sarah says i can send one picture
daisy is sitting on your blanket and mark said no muddy paws
Tell Daisy move please. Also don't touch my shiny stickers.
i only touched the blue one. sarah said snack when you get back
Tyler wants to know if he can push the last button after your song.
Only the quiet one. I got to the end without stopping today.
He clapped with his dinosaur. I marked the chart before he could scribble on it.
Can I try the page with the big jump after lunch if he watches from the couch?
Before we do the bridge, can you scoop the little bricks off the living room rug?
I got most of them. Tyler put the red ones in his truck.
Good. Also your blue folder is under the table, and those new laces are still in the Target bag.
I need the folder for tomorrow. Are the laces for my black shoes?
Dad the tall part tipped again and Tyler drove the red car through the road.
Leave it on the tray. I will check the bottom pieces when I get in.
Mom said I can wait on the porch with her because my hands were all tight.
Good plan. Keep the long gray pieces out and tell Tyler the cars stay on the rug.
Before church, can you bring me the white envelope from the fridge clip?
The one with the house picture stamp?
Yes. Just set it by my purse, please. You do not need to open it.
Ok I put it there and got my shoes.
Mom said I can sit by you after the songs if I use my quiet hands.
Only if you don't make car noises in the pew again.
I will whisper them. Mom packed crackers.
Whispering still counts if Mrs. Jensen turns around.
Melissa did better on the second try with the page today. Slower was easier to hear.
I squeezed my pencil too hard at first.
Tomorrow we can pause at the star sticker, take one breath, and keep going.
My mom said we can draw menus at recess. I am making a castle cafe.
I am making a pizza page with red, yellow, green, and black squares on top.
Put the tiny red circles too. Those are easy to draw.
And yellow fruit pieces. The crunchy green stuff is better when it is on the cheese.
My mom said I can bring the green marker tomorrow. Can your forest page have the secret door?
Yes and then my sentence goes after Ava's. I hope I don't forget it when the big light is on.
You can look at the sticker on your card first. That helped at practice.
Okay. I will say it small if I have to.
I can get you from the west doors at 3:12 tomorrow, then we have time to grab cleats before the field.
Can we also stop for glue sticks? Mrs. Bell said mine is almost gone.
Yep. Backpack first, store second, field third. Bring the reader book so it is not waiting until bedtime.
I will. The outside air felt like recess again today.
Tyler wanted to send this: 'show me your paper with the boxes.'
It is my number boxes. I have to do the last row after snack.
He is making car noises next to you, but I reminded him your pencil space is yours.
He can look if he does not bump me. Mrs. Bell said we use quiet voices for helping.
At recess Jayden said the new kid couldn't be in castle because she didn't know our story.
That made my stomach mad. We can make her the map helper so she has a job.
Can the two sisters find the sparkly trees after school tomorrow?
Yes, but first they have to leave the castle and follow the tiny brown pieces.
Mrs. Bell said tomorrow we can draw one rule for the playground board.
I will draw the map at recess.
Mine is everyone gets a turn and nobody gets left on the bench.
I made a place for it next to the space rocket so they can go really far.
My mom said I can listen on speaker if you do the castle song part.
I can do the first part. The middle still gets mixed up when my fingers cross.
Do the first part then. I will draw a crown on your paper after.
Okay. I want the crown by the line I fixed.
Melissa did well bringing the nurse envelope to my desk. I told her you would read it with her at home.
I did not open it because I was not sure what the little boxes meant
That was a good choice. Let your mom or dad read it, and Nurse Kelly can answer the school part tomorrow.
Melissa, I put your story basket by Table 3. You and Emma may read the first page before cleanup.
Melissa brought back the castle book and told me she read past the picture pages by herself.
Can Ava hold the blue castle card while we read? She made the river part.
The next one has a forest path and a little crown on the cover.
Yes, that works. Please help everyone choose one piece before the bell.
Good choice. If the rain keeps recess inside tomorrow, you may read at the blue table before centers.
Can I ask you if I get worried before recess
Okay. I will give Ben the fox card because he waited.
Can I tell Emma about the funny snow man part after centers if I finish?
Melissa did well reading today. I put the green folder in her backpack for Sarah or Mark to initial tonight.
Can I show Tyler the poem before I bring it back?
Yes, just keep it in the folder after. Daisy paw prints on homework are funny only once.
You may bring your folded book tomorrow if you want to share one page during free choice.
Melissa may like the butterfly life-cycle clip we watched today. I sent the link to Sarah.
Can I show the page where the rocket lands by the tiny animal hospital?
Can I watch it again at home and draw the chrysalis?
That page is fine. Please copy your sentence slowly so your classmates can read the sign.
Ask Sarah first, then pause and sketch the four parts in order.
Melissa did a careful job putting her name stick in for tomorrow's line leader choice.
I will make the sign bigger. The little blocks keep falling off the roof.
She told me two kids wanted the same job and she remembered to wait quietly.
Melissa left her water bottle near the blacktop after recess today.
Thanks, I will have her check her backpack when she gets home.
Yes. We kept the focus on taking turns and saying something kind after the count.
She and Emma were using the cones again, so it may be by the grass line.
That sounds like the right place. She comes home with grass in her shoes a lot lately.
Sarah, Melissa's nurse card came back complete. No extra instructions needed for field day.
Can I still bring my blue water bottle and sit by Emma on the bus?
Yes. I kept the note about taking two quiet breaths before reading, just like assembly practice.
Okay. I can do it if I don't rush the first sentence.
Mrs. Bell sent home the blue folder. I tucked the permission slip back in after signing the next two Tuesdays.
Does that mean I can keep going with Emma?
Yes. Coach wrote that you listened well and tried the passing game after you warmed up.
Can I put the silver sticker on the folder because that was the good note?
Dr. Kemper said your ear looks fine. Put the pink paper in your folder so Mrs. Bell sees it tomorrow.
The nurse sticker is still on my sleeve. She said I was brave.
She was right. Dad is picking up soup, then we will still make it to Wednesday church supper.
Can I sit by you if the room is loud?
My grandma found a recipe card like yours for the class family table. Mine has apple bars.
Mom said we can bring Great-Grandma Ingram's kringla one if I don't spill glue on it.
My mom said we can't get the sparkle stickers today either.
Mrs. Bell said write the story in our own words, not copy the grown-up cursive.
I was mad for a little bit. I put them on my list and drew a castle sticker page.
Can we make the castle have shiny windows at recess Monday?
I can read the card but the old letters make the k look funny.
Yes. I also found two dimes in my coat and put them with my other ones.
Melissa, I put the Bavaria picture page in your take-home folder since you asked to copy the towers carefully.
Thank you. I want to put it beside my map with California on the other side.
That sounds like a good compare-and-contrast page. Remember to write slowly so your place names fit.
I will. I saved room for the car road and the airplane line.
I saw you touch your card, take a breath, and get your words out.
It came out quiet but Mrs. Bell smiled.
Quiet still counts. Your forest picture looked bright from the bleachers too.
Mom says I can send picture. Daisy is looking at her bowl.
Tell Mom I will do it when I get home from Emma's.
Your pencil zipper thing is by my dinos.
Don't open it. My purple shirt for Monday is in the bag too.
My mom said I can come to the party if it is after lunch.
Good. We can make a castle game and you can sit by me when I open stuff.
Are you still doing the number balloon your mom showed us?
Yes, the shiny 8 one. Mom said it has to fit in the car from Council Bluffs.
After my party my mom said we can have the pink drink if your mom says yes.
Mine has to push the loud part. I can put in the banana pieces though.
Good because I want the red berries too, not the green one my cousin had.
Red berries and banana is the best kind.
I can take you to the creek path after I finish the mower belt.
Can I wear boots and see if the tiny frogs are back?
Boots are fine. You stay on my side of the path, especially by the gravel road.
I will. I want to show Tyler the smooth rock but I will wait for you.
I left the little receipt on the hall table. If Mom asks, tell her I already stopped by the office.
Is it the tiny yellow paper?
That's it. Leave it under the magnet so it does not blow away when Tyler runs past.
I used the soccer magnet.
Grab your sweater before we leave. The Ingram pew row fills up fast when the Nelsons get there early.
Can I sit by Tyler if he doesn't make car sounds?
Deal. Afterward we'll stop at Casey's; I bet we'll run into someone from school there too.
Can you put on the song with the stomping before we go?
Melissa told me at pack-up she wanted to sign the spring field sheet herself.
She asked me this morning where the pen was, then changed her mind twice.
I let her keep it on her desk until recess. Emma checked her own box first, and Melissa did hers right after.
That sounds like her. We will put the cleats by the door tonight.
Melissa did well with the snack sorting activity today. She kept choosing the red, yellow, green, and purple pieces first.
That sounds like her. We use rows like that on pizza nights too.
That makes sense. She told her table the green pieces are easier when they sit on melted cheese.
Your LEGO bridge can wait on the tray until after bath. We will leave the porch light on for a quick run first.
Can I show you the first paragraph before I run?
Yes. One try, then shoes. If your hands get buzzy, come get a squeeze.
I want the squeeze after the paragraph.
I changed the channel after the supper headlines. You didn't miss anything you need for second grade.
The red and blue signs by Casey's are not soccer teams?
Nope, just grown-up sign stuff. You can ask Mom or me when something sounds confusing.
Okay. I like Mrs. Bell's way better when we just count the sticks and clap.
I put your lunch card in the front pocket. Bus line leaves at 7:42, so shoes before the cereal is gone.
Can I take my purple notebook for the story part?
Yes. Mrs. Bell also wrote that you need to listen for the directions before starting the first page.
I will wait until she says go.
Mom typing: Tyler says sorry for touching the shiny stickers.
He bent the purple one and then my tower fell when he bumped the chair.
Mom typing: He can put his dinosaur by the couch until Dad checks the tower.
Okay. I want Mom by me while I fix the sticker page.
At recess Monday can we start at the swings and make the castle road go past the big tree?
Yes and the cones can be the gate. We have to get there before the boys take them.
Then after that we can do the chasing part if the grass is not too wet.
I want the part where we go around the tree twice.
Mom said Dr. Jensen checked the chart and the next little arm pinch is not until fall.
Good because it hurt for one second
You still sat still. If you wonder why the paper has another date, ask Mom after supper and she can show you the chart.
Can you ask her with me
The bridge stayed up with three books on it. Pretty solid.
Good because the moon people have to drive over it to get to the castle.
I set the flat gray pieces back by the couch. Roads can go there after supper.
Do not move the little green tunnel. That is the secret way for the sisters.
Melissa, your note for sharing circle is in your folder. Remember: one sentence per box, slow pencil.
I wrote that schools should have crayons that are not broken and books for every desk.
That is clear. You may add one sentence about what grown-ups should do when someone says a rule hurt them.
They should listen first and make it so everybody can feel safe in the game.
Melissa, your class drawing of the nest by the oak was careful work. Please keep your group on the blacktop until I call table two.
Can I add the speckled eggs after recess? I saw them when we lined up.
Yes, after recess. If you want another look, ask me first and we will stand where I can see the door.
You did a good job asking before you left the line for your water bottle today.
Melissa left her purple folder by the reading rug. I sent it with Emma because I saw both families by the milk cooler yesterday.
I remembered what Officer Martin said about finding a grown-up with a badge or a teacher.
Thank you. Emma said we might sing the arm-waving one again this weekend.
That was exactly the right plan. Your note is in the front pocket for your mom.
That one has a good steady beat for remembering words. Slow down on the second verse like you do in class.
I told Emma I was not scared, just forgot which door was ours.
Mom says I can send this. Can my red car go in your fort road?
Yes but don't smash the bridge. Emma and me are making two roads so yours can have a tunnel.
I will not smash. I want the dinosaur by the tree.
Okay, the dinosaur can guard the pine trees. You can put three cars after we finish the river.
Mom says no outside. I made cars on couch.
Tyler wants to hear the frog song too, so share the tablet nicely.
Mom says I can send this. Vroom. I put my red car on your space road.
I only have two songs left before the timer beeps.
Do not put them on my book. I am where the kids find the door in the tree.
Do not crash it into the white building. That is where the sick puppy goes.
froggy one again please
Can we watch cowboy man and rocket man?
I made dinosaur wait outside.
After the beep, put it on the counter and both of you can build roads.
Only if Mom says yes after bath stuff.
Good. I still need to put the paper sign and the new moon window on it.
Grandma handed me your card envelope. Want it on your dresser or with Mom?
Dresser please. The paper money can fold and the coins can go in the slot.
Got it. We are still just looking at that big LEGO kit today.
Okay. I will copy the picture when we get home so I can put it on my list.
I found the little state map you left in the truck. Want it back for your wall?
Yes please. I need the long line from Iowa to Anaheim, then the other one across the ocean.
We can tape yarn for both after supper. Tyler already grabbed the blue roll.
Can we use red for the car one from last Saturday too?
Mom says do not color on the papers by the toaster.
I know. Those are not drawing papers.
She said we can use the dinosaur book instead.
We can stop at Hy-Vee in Council Bluffs after soccer and look for the April 12 plates.
Can they have stars? Emma likes stars too.
Stars are fine. Keep your shin guards in the Neola bag so we do not lose them.
Mom is still at the store. Please do not start the kitchen machine before she gets back.
I just got the cup and the banana out.
That is fine. Leave the frozen berries in the bag for now so the counter does not get sticky.
Mom says show me kick after bath
Only if you don't peel the glitter ones off my water bottle.
I want tiger sticker
You can have one paper star, not the team one. I need my guards packed for Tuesday.
My mom said I can go to the field if I finish my math page. Are you going after pickup?
Not today. Mom said store first and then I have the next two reading pages.
Tomorrow we can do castle tag at recess. Did you remember the song words?
Yes. Mrs. Bell had us stand by the stage tape again and it was brighter by the windows.
Sarah told me you stayed with the tricky line yesterday. Bring your little chart tomorrow if you want to show me.
Can I show the part with the two hands? It is not fast yet.
Yes. Slow and careful is fine. I will put it by your story folder so you remember.
I want Emma to see the new sticker too.
Mom typed this. Show me the kick again after bath.
Only if you do not drive cars through the cones.
I will make car noises quiet. You can be the teacher.
Okay. I can show the slow one Emma showed me.
I set your folder on the kitchen chair. Mom put the family-tree sheet beside it.
Do I write Ingram on Dad's side and Miller on Mom's side?
Yep. Ask Grandma Sarah about the Miller farm before supper if you want one more detail.
I already wrote about the library lunch and the old recipe card.
My mom said I can ask if you got the same take-home book today.
Yes, the frog one. We have to read it and put three words on the lines.
Do you want to be my table buddy again when we do the blocks on Monday?
Yes. I will share the tens blocks if you share the long ones.
Can you play castles after supper or do you have soccer?
My mom said I have to give the yellow paper to Nurse Kelly Monday.
After supper maybe. Sarah said first I have to put my shoes by the door and feed Daisy.
My mom said grownups were picking stuff today so I asked if we get stickers too.
I gave mine to Mrs. Bell first because I did not know what it meant
I only got a sticker when our table picked the extra recess game.
Okay. I have to ask my grandma. Is Tyler still making car noises?
Did it have the tiny arm picture
Mrs. Bell said tomorrow we can choose between kickball and chalk if nobody argues.
Yes but Mom said Dr. Jensen already told us what to do so I stopped guessing
Yes and Mark told him cars stay off my reading book.
My mom got the picture of your rainbow fox. It was cute.
I hope chalk wins but I won't be mad. She said kind faces after the count.
I followed the fox drawing steps on the tablet before dinner.
Can you send me the steps?
Mom said she will send it when I am done putting pajamas on.
Did your castle stay up after school?
No because Tyler put a car on the gate. I went to Mom in the laundry room.
My little cousin does that with blocks too.
Dad said the gate needs two flat pieces under it, so I am saving it for tomorrow.
I put the blue plates back in the LEGO bin. Bridge repair crew is ready after supper.
Thanks. The new soccer drill made my legs feel jumpy before we started.
You still tried it. Build for ten minutes, then we can kick at the fence twice.
Ok, but I want to practice the kick slow first.
I found your shin guards. Coach only asked for water, shoes, and that signed packet.
No extra paper from Mom?
Nope. Same packet from the clinic. If the first drill feels too fast, take a breath and watch Emma's feet.
Okay. I want to try the passing line again.
I'm picking up Casey's on the way back. Want me to ask for your corner with the red, yellow, green, and black toppings?
Yes, and the little meat circles.
Got it. Pineapple too, or skip it tonight?
Pineapple too. It goes by the yellow pieces.
Emma asked if anybody in our family ever had to wear the clinky wrist things from movies.
Not anyone close to us, kiddo. Movies make lots of things look more common than they are.
So Uncle Ben and Mrs. Reed from church didn't?
Nope. And if you have big questions, ask me, Mom, Mrs. Bell, or Dr. Kemper. We will answer plainly.
I found two flat gray pieces for the launch door. They are on the workbench by the tape.
Thank you. The door has to open so the little cart can bring the hurt cat inside.
Use the wider base under it first. Then your paper front can stand up without bending.
Then it will match the last page better.
Melissa, Sarah said you may bring the small envelope for our classroom store tomorrow, but keep it zipped until morning meeting.
I only want to look. I am keeping my chore dollar at home this time.
That works. If the scented eraser is gone, you can sketch it in your notebook and we will check the next store day.
Okay. I have a spot for it on the back page.
Melissa, I put your take-home page in the front pocket after reading groups.
Thank you. I found my pouch after recess. It was in the coat cubby.
Good find. Please remember the book for Monday, and tell your mom the spring picture shirt came home in your backpack.
I put your yellow notebook by the back door for the sunset colors.
Thank you. If the stray cat comes by the lilacs can I sit on the steps and draw him?
Steps are okay. Tell me before you go past the lilacs, and do not walk toward Maple Street.
I will stay on the steps. I like when the wind moves the notebook pages.
Emma's mom said 9:30 works tomorrow before the church lunch. Please put the markers back in the box tonight.
Can we make cards for the neighbor's new puppy and then do the fairy trail with Tyler?
Yes, if the table is clear first. Save two jobs for Tyler so he doesn't just grab.
He can stamp paws and Emma can draw the gate. I will write the puppy's name slow.
Bath in ten. Please pause before the whole floor is covered.
I just need to put the white tower by the rocket place.
One tower, then lights out. I left the shoebox lid by your bed for tiny pieces.
The trail pieces go in there too so the sisters can find them tomorrow.
Mom says I can send one. I made car roads by the porch.
Do not put them in my trail under the bushes.
Can you show me the big kick after dinner?
Only if you race from the porch to the fence with me first.
My mom said the field is too muddy. Are you doing couch day too?
Maybe after I read one more chapter. The sisters are at the icy stairs now.
Tell me Monday if they get out. Did your mom pick the movie yet?
She said maybe the one with the songs if Tyler stops jumping.
We passed the people by the courthouse. Thank you for staying with me on the sidewalk and not trying to squeeze into the crowd.
I just read the big sign words again. I still don't know all of it.
That's okay. You asked a careful question. What did you think the sign wanted?
For people to be nicer, and for helpers to keep everybody safe, not just some people.
We have enough strawberries for one cup after church, but only if you help me wipe the counter first.
Can it have banana too?
Yes. You can drop the pieces in after I plug it in and stand beside you.
I will wait by the stool.
Did you see the weather tomorrow?
Yeah, rain all day apparently
Want me to grab anything from the store?
We need paper towels if you pass Target
My wifi has been terrible today
Same, I restarted the router twice
Can you remind me to call back tomorrow?
Setting a reminder now
Left my sunglasses somewhere again
Check the car, you always leave them there
printer is jammed again
Try pulling the tray all the way out
picking up coffee, want one?
Yes please, the usual
Are you coming to the thing on Friday?
Maybe, depends on work
Did the package arrive?
Yeah it is by the door
Can I borrow your charger?
It is in the kitchen drawer
